result: CRISPR/Cas9-based crispant screening achieved high indel efficiency (mean 88%, minimum 71%) with out-of-frame rates of 49-73%, resulting in 60-92% of reads with likely loss-of-function indels. Off-target analysis showed no mutations in 20 of 30 sites examined, with remaining sites showing 0.11-2.82% off-target rates.
evaluation: All reviewers affirmed the high mutagenic efficacy and technical validity of the CRISPR approach. Reviewer 1 stated 'the effectiveness of the method is evaluated to 60% to 92% of the respective target genes being presumably inactivated' and Reviewer 2 noted 'NGS was performed on embryos injected with different gRNAs/Cas9 to confirm high mutagenic efficacy, and off-target cutting was verified to be low.' No concerns were raised about these technical measurements.

result: Larval crispants at 7 and 14 dpf showed variable phenotypes in osteoblast-positive areas and mineralized surfaces. esr1 and ifitm5 crispants exhibited increased osteoblast-positive surface area, while aldh7a1 and sec24d showed reduced mineralized surface in the head. Several crispants showed altered mineralization at the notochord tip and opercle.
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledged these findings but expressed concerns about their interpretation. Reviewer 2 noted that 'Measurements of surface area covered by osteoblasts or mineralized bone (Fig. 1) are typically normalized to body size...This was not done here' and that 'the reader is not given the opportunity to consider whether earlier differences in, e.g. surface area covered by osteoblasts at 14 dpf, could be accounted for by delayed or accelerated overall growth.' Reviewer 3 noted 'the variability of developmental phenotypes' as a weakness. The lack of normalization and high variability reduce confidence in these larval findings.

result: RT-qPCR analysis at 7 and 14 dpf revealed differential expression of osteogenic markers. runx2 remained unchanged across timepoints, while bglap was downregulated in most crispants at both timepoints. col1a1a was upregulated in several crispants at 7 dpf, with patterns persisting or normalizing by 14 dpf. sp7 showed gene-specific changes.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted the molecular findings as valid. Reviewer 1 noted that 'the osteoblast-positive areas are more often affected in the crispants compared to the mineralized areas, an observation that appears to correlate with the observed reduced expression of bglap, a marker for mature osteoblasts, and the increased expression of col1a1a in more immature osteoblasts.' The correlation between phenotypic and molecular data was viewed positively, though reviewers noted caveats about interpretation related to genetic compensation.

result: aldh7a1 and mbtps2 crispants displayed early lethality. aldh7a1 crispants showed increased mortality from 7 dpf with no survivors beyond 20 dpf, while mbtps2 crispants exhibited increased lethality from 17 dpf with very few surviving to adulthood. Surviving mbtps2 adults showed severe cranial malformations.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted these mortality findings without challenge. Reviewer 1 noted 'the injected fish (except two lines that revealed a high mortality) are also analyzed at 90dpf' and Reviewer 2 acknowledged 'two of the lines were larval-lethal.' The severe phenotypes leading to lethality were treated as valid observations supporting the functional importance of these genes.

result: Adult crispants (90 dpf) showed no differences in standard length and head size, except esr1 crispants with larger eye diameters. All crispants except daam2 displayed vertebral abnormalities including fusions, fractures, and arch malformations. MicroCT analysis revealed altered centrum volume, TMD, thickness, and length in specific crispants, with daam2, esr1, and sost showing increased TMD.
evaluation: Reviewers strongly affirmed the adult skeletal phenotypes. Reviewer 1 stated the study 'makes a compelling case for using the crispant technology to screen the function of candidate genes' and noted 'increased incidence of skeletal deformities in the vertebral arches, fractures, as well as vertebral fusions and compressions.' Reviewer 2 emphasized 'Convincing data demonstrate the feasibility and validity of this approach.' The adult phenotypes were viewed as the most robust and reproducible findings, with Reviewer 3 noting 'a major strength of the paper is the streamlined method that produced significant phenotypes for all candidate genes tested.'

result: Skeletal malformations in crispants were reproducible across independent clutches, and all studied crispants exhibited skeletal abnormalities in adult stages, demonstrating the feasibility of the crispant approach for identifying genes implicated in skeletal disorders.
evaluation: Reviewers affirmed the reproducibility and overall success of the approach. Reviewer 1 stated 'All my issues were resolved' and noted the manuscript 'makes a compelling case for using the crispant technology.' Reviewer 2 emphasized the study 'presents an important tool for rapid functional validation of candidate gene(s)' and noted 'Convincing data demonstrate the feasibility and validity of this approach.' The reproducibility across clutches strengthened confidence in the methodology.

result: Ten candidate genes were selected for analysis: six genes associated with recessive osteogenesis imperfecta (CREB3L1, MBTPS2, SPARC, SERPINF1, IFITM5, SEC24D) and four genes associated with bone mineral density from GWAS studies (ALDH7A1, ESR1, DAAM2, SOST).
evaluation: While reviewers accepted the gene selection rationale, Reviewer 3 raised concerns about incomplete characterization of gene features that might affect crispant phenotypes: 'do genes with maternally deposited transcript exhibit dampened phenotypes? Or does genetic compensation impact certain genes more than others? Since authors state that the study represents a methods paper, it will be important for users to understand the caveats of gene selection to effectively implement and interpret results of the approach.' This suggests the gene selection criteria and their implications were not fully addressed.

result: The crispant approach offers advantages over stable lines including shorter generation time (~3 months vs 6-9 months). Previous studies demonstrated that crispants for lrp5, bmp1a, and plod2 showed phenotypic similarity to stable knockout or germline mutant lines.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted the rationale and validation of the crispant approach based on prior work. Reviewer 1 noted 'this is done for some of the tested genes as laid out in the discussion' when addressing the lack of germline validation in the current study. The cited precedents were not challenged, supporting the methodological foundation.
